en.name: Tapioca pearls, cooked
en.summary: Cooked tapioca pearls keep 1–2 days in the refrigerator at 5 °C or below, and that is an outer limit rather than a plan — the pearls go hard and cloudy within hours of chilling. Cook what you will drink today.
en.pantry: Cooked pearls sitting in warm syrup on a counter are a wet cooked starch, and they carry the same Bacillus cereus risk as a pot of cooked rice: the spores survive boiling, they germinate as the syrup cools through the danger zone, and the emetic toxin they can produce is not destroyed by reheating. Tea shops keep a batch for a few hours at most, but that is a texture rule about chew, not a food-safety allowance you can borrow for a pot left out all afternoon at home. Either hold them genuinely hot, above 60 °C, or chill them.
en.fridge: Refrigerated storage of cooked starchy food of this kind is capped at about 1–2 days at 5 °C or below. Store the pearls in their syrup in a covered container so they do not dry out, and be realistic about what you will get back: they harden and go cloudy in the fridge within hours as the starch retrogrades, and a spell in the microwave or a dip in hot syrup only partly revives them. The honest advice is to boil a small batch each time rather than to store any.
en.freezer: There is no freezer entry for cooked tapioca pearls because freezing them does not work. Ice crystals wreck the gel structure completely, and thawed pearls come back grainy, split and chalky in the middle — inedible rather than merely disappointing. If you want tapioca on hand, keep the uncooked dry pearls in the cupboard, which store very well, and boil them as you need them.
spoilage: A sour or fermented smell from the syrup.
Syrup that has gone cloudy, ropy or is bubbling.
A slimy film on the pearls, or pearls stuck in a solid mass.
Any mould on the surface of the syrup.
tips: Boil only what you will drink in one session.
Hold pearls hot above 60 °C or chill them; do not leave them warm.
Store them in their syrup, covered, so they do not dry out.
Keep dry uncooked pearls in the cupboard for convenience instead of storing cooked ones.

faq.q: How long do cooked boba pearls keep?
faq.a: 1–2 days at 5 °C or below, and they will already be hard and cloudy long before that. Cook them fresh.

faq.q: Can you freeze cooked tapioca pearls?
faq.a: No. Freezing destroys the gel and they thaw grainy and chalky. Store the uncooked dry pearls instead.

faq.q: Is it safe to leave boba in warm syrup on the counter?
faq.a: No. Wet cooked starch left warm grows Bacillus cereus, and reheating does not remove the toxin it can produce. Hold them above 60 °C or refrigerate them.

zh.name: 熟珍珠
zh.summary: 煮好的珍珠冷藏 5 °C 以下可放 1～2 天，但那是上限而不是計畫——珍珠冰進冰箱幾小時內就會變硬、變濁。今天要喝多少就煮多少。
zh.pantry: 煮好的珍珠泡在溫糖水裡放在檯面上，就是一份含水的熟澱粉，帶著和一鍋熟飯一樣的仙人掌桿菌風險：孢子撐得過滾煮，糖水降溫經過危險溫度帶時它們開始萌發，而它們可能產生的嘔吐型毒素，並不會因為再加熱而消失。飲料店一批珍珠最多留幾個小時，但那是關於口感的規則，不是可以套用到家裡「放一下午」的食安額度。要嘛真的保溫在 60 °C 以上，要嘛就冰起來。
zh.fridge: 這一類熟澱粉食品的冷藏上限大約是 5 °C 以下 1～2 天。請連糖水一起裝進加蓋容器，免得表面乾掉；同時也要務實面對它的狀態：澱粉老化讓珍珠在冰箱裡幾小時內就變硬、變濁，微波一下或泡回熱糖水也只能救回一部分。誠實的建議是：每次煮一小鍋，不要想著存放。
zh.freezer: 熟珍珠沒有冷凍欄位，因為冷凍根本行不通。冰晶會徹底破壞它的凝膠結構，解凍後的珍珠又粗又裂、中心粉白——那是不能吃，而不只是不好吃。想要隨時有珍珠，請把「生粉圓」放在櫥櫃，它非常耐放，要喝再煮。
spoilage: 糖水聞起來發酸或有發酵味。
糖水變混濁、牽絲或在冒泡。
珍珠表面出現黏滑薄膜，或黏成一整塊。
tips: 一次只煮這一輪喝得完的量。
要嘛保溫在 60 °C 以上，要嘛冰起來，不要停在溫溫的狀態。
連糖水一起加蓋保存，避免表面乾硬。
想方便就在櫥櫃常備生粉圓，而不是存熟的。

faq.q: 煮好的珍珠可以放多久？
faq.a: 5 °C 以下 1～2 天，而且遠在那之前就已經變硬變濁了。建議現煮現喝。
不行。冷凍會毀掉凝膠結構，解凍後又粗又白。請改存生的乾粉圓。

faq.q: 珍珠泡在溫糖水放檯面上安全嗎？
faq.a: 不安全。溫著的熟澱粉會長仙人掌桿菌，而再加熱也去不掉它產生的毒素。請保溫在 60 °C 以上或冷藏。
